newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu says will block settler enclave.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu says will block settler enclave.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has told the Palestinian Authority that he will block building of a Jewish settler enclave in the heart of Arab East Jerusalem "at this time", his office said on Friday.
"As of now, the decision is not to let it go ahead and that is precisely what is going to happen," David Bar-Illan, Netanyahu's communications chief, told Israel Radio.

He said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had received the assurance on Thursday night in a telephone call from a senior Netanyahu aide, Yitzhak Molho, and "was quite pleased to hear the explanation".
Arafat aides were not immediately available for comment.

Construction of the few dozen houses by American Jewish magnate Irving Moskowitz in the 11,000-strong Arab neighbourhood of Ras al-Amoud was given the green light by the Israeli Jerusalem municipality on Thursday night.
The surprise move had prompted indignation from Palestinian officials and warnings that construction could ignite fresh violence.
Arafat's adviser, Ahmed Tibi, branded it a "declaration of war" and a violation of interim peace deals signed by Israel and Arafat's PLO since 1993.

Netanyahu's peace talks with the PLO have been in crisis since March when Israel broke ground on Har Homa settlement on a hilltop known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim on the edge of East Jerusalem.
Arafat has insisted that work there must stop before substantive negotiations can resume.

Bar-Illan said Netanyahu believed the time was not right to build at Ras al-Amoud given that the project was in the midst of a densely-populated Arab neighbourhood and given the state of peace negotiations.
He said there was no question of a similar freeze at Har Homa. "It's a barren hill, it's near two Jewish neighbourhoods and it is not in anyone's way," Bar-Illan told Reuters.
The status of East Jerusalem, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Middle East War, is one of the most volatile issues dividing Israelis and Palestinians.

The PLO wants East Jerusalem as capital of a future Palestinian state and says Israeli moves are aimed at pre-empting talks on the city's fate. Israel says both sides of the city form its "united and eternal" capital.

Israel's Jerusalem municipal planning commission gave conditional approval last December to a plan for 132 settler homes on a 3.5 acre (1.4 hectare) plot at Ras al-Amoud, which overlooks the walled Old City of Jerusalem.
The plan required the approval of Interior Minister Eli Suissa but was later shelved.
Mayor Ehud Olmert, a member of Netanyahu's Likud bloc, said the plan approved on Thursday was for a scaled-down project.

He said he doubted that Moskowitz, a Miami-based businessman who bankrolls Jewish settlement in occupied areas, would go ahead with the scheme as approved because the American, who had threatened legal action, would fight for the bigger project.
Bar-Illan said Netanyahu did not contest Moskowitz's right to build on the plot under Israeli law but questioned the advisability of doing so "at this time, and I stress at this time".
"There are means by which the government can prevent this building...It can invoke a national interest and security reasons," he said.
